topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines student backgrounds, and establishes the foundational learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular and Developmental Foundations of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as a progressive failure of normal differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes, alongside experimental models used to study these cellular behaviors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Histological Features of Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the transition of tumors from benign confined growths to invasive and metastatic malignancies, highlighting histological identification using colorectal cancer progression as a model.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature, Clinical Behavior, and Pathological Impacts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the standard naming conventions for different tumor types and explain the specific physiological mechanisms through which benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and Comparative Oncology Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence and tissue vulnerabilities in human populations and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles, histological detection methods, and clinical effectiveness of screening programs designed to identify pre-malignant lesions in various organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the session by revisiting the core learning outcomes and giving directions for upcoming practicals.
